summary: Data-driven dialect registry. Defines the DialectSpec dataclass plus the UpsertStyle, TransactionSupport, DropScope, IndexCapability and SessionOption types, one connection-builder function per dialect, per-dialect transaction probes (SQLite in_transaction, DuckDB txid_current comparison, psycopg transaction_status), the SQLite DELETE-based truncate hook, DuckDB adoption session options, and the DIALECTS mapping of 20 dialect keys (sqlite, duckdb, motherduck, postgres, mysql, mssql, oracle, snowflake, bigquery, redshift, trino, clickhouse, databricks, singlestoredb, exasol, impala, materialize, risingwave, druid, pyspark). IbisBackend reads every capability decision from this table.
extension_points: Add a dialect by adding a DIALECTS entry with a connection_builder and capability fields
Override generic operations per dialect via upsert_hook, add_columns_hook, rename_table_hook, truncate_table_hook, create_index_hook, drop_index_hook, list_indexes_hook
ibis_connection_adapter post-processes a built ibis connection (used by Exasol)
adoption_mutations declares session options to snapshot/restore on raw adoption
transaction_support, begin_statement, begin_hook, in_transaction_probe, precommit_probe, raw_execute_hook tune transaction behaviour
lifecycle_notes: DIALECTS is built once at import time; DialectSpec is frozen
Connection builders pass credentials as driver kwargs, never URL userinfo, and route failures through connect_redacted so secrets are not echoed
operations and _index_inspection are imported at the bottom of the module (noqa E402) to break the operations <-> dialects import cycle
documentation_hooks: Support matrix: per-dialect upsert style, index capability, transaction support and adoption verification
Why credentials are passed as kwargs rather than URL userinfo
risks: No in-tree dialect sets upsert_hook, add_columns_hook, rename_table_hook, create_index_hook or drop_index_hook; these seams are untested by a real consumer
DialectSpec.connection_mode and extras are populated but never read by any source module
Oracle compat is applied inside _build_oracle_connection rather than via ibis_connection_adapter, so Oracle connections adopted via from_ibis_connection are not patched
Circular import with operations is resolved by a bottom-of-module import; reordering imports can break module load
databricks has connection_string_scheme='' which produces an empty-string key in the URL scheme reverse map
motherduck declares TransactionSupport.FULL without an in_transaction_probe; it is outside OWNERSHIP_DIALECTS so it uses plain BEGIN/COMMIT
open_questions: Should connection_mode and extras be removed or wired into dispatch?
Should Oracle patching move to ibis_connection_adapter so adopted connections receive it?

evidence.detail: raw_adoption_verified=True only on duckdb and motherduck
